result.title: GazeLens for Efficient Egocentric Video Question Answering with Simple Gaze-Driven Adaptive Token Reduction
result.summary: Smart glasses can help users understand their activities and surroundings, but small vision-language models must preserve useful evidence within limited computation. This is difficult because redundant frames consume the visual budget, while aggressive spatial compression can discard relevant details. Although gaze identifies the wearer's focus, the question may require evidence from the surrounding scene. To address these constraints, we propose GazeLens, which combines frame selection with gaze- and question-guided token reduction. First, HOG transitions and image sharpness select frames before visual encoding. For each selected frame, Gaussian pooling then forms gaze-focused and complementary summaries. Because their relevance depends on the question, a lightweight gate blends them into a primary token. Together with a global scene token, this retains both focused and contextual summaries within two tokens per frame. On StreamGaze, GazeLens achieves higher macro and micro accuracy than the evaluated full-grid and token-reduction baselines, with lower input-forward FLOPs than the shared-backbone token-reduction baselines.

AI.brief_summary: GazeLens 面向智能眼镜上的第一人称视频问答，先用 HOG 转场与图像清晰度选帧，再对每帧做注视与问题引导的高斯池化，生成聚焦与互补摘要并用轻量门控融合，配合全局场景 token 将每帧压到两个 token，在 StreamGaze 上以更低 FLOPs 超过所比较的 token 缩减基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关联「视觉证据筛选」与有限视觉预算下的推理成本问题，可供核查注视引导压缩是否保留任务必要细节、以及聚焦/全局双 token 是否造成信息坍缩；但压缩位于视觉编码输入侧而非 latent 推理状态生成，故优先级较低。
